summary: Luboš Bělka is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from around 1978 to 1983 and later held an academic post there around 1993.
Luca Brigada Villa works in the fields of linguistics and computational linguistics. He has held academic posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.

Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin (2005–2010), served as director of IsMEO around 2013, and became Associate Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice around 2021.

Lucia Dolce specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held posts at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and Associate Professor (attested 2015), and is attested as a visiting researcher at Minobusan University (2026).
Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her doctorate and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.

Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at the University of Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a professor at Munich (c. 1901–1933) and directed the Museum Fünf Kontinente (1907).

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught at Allahabad, held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984), and served as IATS President (c. 1989–1995).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl was a French scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne, founded the Institut d'ethnologie, and held a post at the University of Paris from around 1899 to 1927.

Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig University, and under Antoine Meillet. He held academic posts at the universities of Ljubljana (1920–1924), Strasbourg (1924–1937), and Montpellier (1937).
Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University, where she was supervised by Anne C. Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

Indologist Ludo Rocher studied at Ghent University and under scholars including Adriaan Scharpé and Jan Gonda. He served as Professor at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and later as Chair and Emeritus Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2016).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD under Walther Schubring at Hamburg and completed his habilitation under Heinrich Lüders at Berlin. He taught at Berlin and Münster before succeeding Schubring as chair at Hamburg (1950–1972).

Ludwig Diestel was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held academic appointments at the universities of Bonn (c. 1858–1862), Greifswald (c. 1862–1867), Jena (c. 1867–1872), and Tübingen (c. 1872–1879).

Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He served as professor at Greifswald (from 1904) and held a post at the University of Tartu (1918).

Ludwig Lange was a classical philologist and historian who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at Charles University (1853–1859), the University of Giessen (1859–1871), and Leipzig University (from 1871), where he served as rector (1879–1880).

Ludwig Ross was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Kiel University (c. 1825–1829). He held academic posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TU Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge, earning his PhD at Cambridge in 1929. He was a fellow and lecturer at Trinity College and professor of philosophy at Cambridge (1930–1947).
Ludwik Skurzak is an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He held an academic post as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

Luigi Suali was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi, and held a long-standing academic post at the University of Pavia from around 1907 to 1951.

Luis O. Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD at Yale under Stanley Insler, served as department chair and professor at the University of Michigan, and was Academic Director at the Mangalam Research Center (c. 2010–2017).
